description.extended:
The German and Russian volume of Hedi Slimane's four-part Anthology of a Decade, the shortest of the set, collecting the black-and-white photographs he made in Berlin and Moscow during the 2000s.

JRP|Ringier published Anthology of a Decade in 2011 as four slipcased softcover volumes, one per territory, edited by Lionel Bovier in an edition of 1,000 and sold singly from 2012. The DE RU book runs to 120 pages with 110 duotone plates. Its subject is young men at military academies in the two cities, photographed on manoeuvres, exercising and resting, in groups and alone, with still lifes and snow scenes from Berlin and Moscow set between them. The cover renders the German tricolour in black, grey and white and reads DE RU, the territory code the set uses in place of a title. JRP|Ringier and D.A.P. list this volume as Europa.

Slimane (b. 1968, Paris) had photographed Berlin before, in Berlin (Steidl/7L, 2003) and in the club and rock pictures of Interzone (Purple Books, 2005). This volume moves away from the music scenes of the other three toward a quieter, more formal study of uniformed youth.
description.artist_bio: Hedi Slimane (b. 1968, Paris) was menswear director at Yves Saint Laurent Rive Gauche (1997-2000), creative director of Dior Homme (2000-2007), Yves Saint Laurent (2012-2016) and Celine (2018-2024), and has run a photography practice throughout, with books including Berlin (Steidl/7L, 2003), Stage (Steidl/7L, 2004), London Birth of a Cult (Steidl, 2005) and Interzone (Purple Books, 2005).

notes: Shelf: Fashion. Volume DE RU of the four-volume Anthology of a Decade (JRP|Ringier, 2011), the others being US (9783037642214), UK (9783037642221) and FR (9783037642238). Also issued as a slipcased set of all four, ISBN 9783037641156 (724 pages). Volumes sold separately from 2012. Listed by JRP|Ringier and D.A.P. as Europa; cover reads DE RU.

research_log.notes: Publisher page and D.A.P. agree on ISBN, pages, 232 x 290 mm, softcover, edition of 1,000, editor Lionel Bovier. Image count from the publisher (110 b/w); D.A.P. gives a slightly different count for the US and UK volumes. Year: the set was issued April 2011 (JRP, Getty); JRP and D.A.P. date the single-volume release February/April 2012. Subtitle taken from the cover as printed (DE RU), not from the trade listing name (Europa). OpenLibrary attaches Vince Aletti and Jon Savage as authors across these ISBNs, which no publisher or Getty record supports, so no essayists are recorded.
